about:
# LuaWorkbench

![LuaWorkbench](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/R41z0r/LuaWorkbench/main/Artwork/Logo.png)

LuaWorkbench is a Lua editor for World of Warcraft. Write and run code in-game, save snippets for later, and keep them organized in folders. It works on its own and does not require another addon.

The editor includes syntax highlighting, code search, and a separate output panel for printed messages, return values and errors. You can also search through all your saved snippets, including their code.

- Run code with the Play button, **Ctrl+Enter**, or **F5**.
- Save with **Ctrl+S**, recover drafts after a reload, or return to the last saved version.
- Run saved scripts at startup, login or on a WoW event you choose.
- Adjust fonts, indentation, bracket completion and the output limit in Options.
- Resize the window, give the code editor more space, or minimize it while you play.

Open it with `/lua`, `/le`, `/luaeditor` or `/luaworkbench`. The **?** button lists the shortcuts and explains the available options.

Supports Retail, Forever and TBC, with translations for all 11 WoW languages.

**Please keep in mind:** This runs real Lua code in your game. Only run scripts you trust. A running script cannot be interrupted; an infinite loop can freeze the game. Automatic runs are off by default. Enable startup, login or a custom WoW event for each script; only its saved code will run.

LuaWorkbench's own code is MIT-licensed. Bundled libraries keep their original licenses and notices. The repository is private during initial development; contributions and translations will be welcome when it opens.

## Installation

Install the shared package for Retail, Forever and TBC into `Interface/AddOns/!!!LuaWorkbench`, then restart the game or reload. Snippets and settings are stored account-wide in `LuaWorkbenchDB`. Draft recovery is enabled by default and can be disabled in Options. Automatic runs are opt-in for each script and use the last saved code.

## Development

```sh
luacheck --no-color -q .
python3 scripts/check_lua_upvalues.py .
python3 scripts/validate_project.py
```

`Localization.lua` contains eleven translations. When adding or changing text, update every locale in the same change. The checks verify matching keys and alphabetical ordering. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/R41z0r/LuaWorkbench/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

Static checks do not replace in-game testing on each supported client.

## Local deployment

```sh
python3 scripts/deploy.py --flavor forever --target "$WOW_ADDONS_DIR"
```

Set `WOW_ADDONS_DIR` to your client’s existing `Interface/AddOns` directory. Supported flavors: `retail`, `forever`, `tbc`. Deployment copies runtime files, assets, bundled libraries and the shared TOC. It does not touch SavedVariables. The convenience `build.sh` used locally is intentionally ignored and is not part of this repository.

## Releases and licenses

See [RELEASING.md](https://github.com/R41z0r/LuaWorkbench/blob/main/docs/RELEASING.md) for the shared changelog and tag-driven uploads to CurseForge and Wago. No release is published by a regular branch push.

Original code and artwork use [MIT](https://github.com/R41z0r/LuaWorkbench/blob/main/LICENSE), attributed to LuaWorkbench contributors. [THIRD_PARTY.md](https://github.com/R41z0r/LuaWorkbench/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY.md) records the separate terms for bundled libraries.

releases.notes:
## [1.2.4] - 2026-11-17

### Fixed

- Refresh typed and deleted code even during repeated native cursor/layout updates.
- Keep the editor caret and current-line highlight aligned with visible code across window heights and wrapped lines.
- Preserve literal pipes and color codes through code entry, paste, selection, saving and execution without rewriting Lua strings.
- Keep syntax colors when resizing the editor reveals more text than fits in one syntax overlay.
- Show relevant script stack frames in error output while retaining the complete captured stack in session diagnostics.
- Include available global and C_ functions missing from Blizzard’s generated documentation in Knowledge Base searches, with a notice when argument and return documentation is unavailable.

## [1.2.3] - 2026-11-14

### Fixed

- Keep detached output windows above editor text and controls.
- Align syntax text and wrapped line numbers with the editor's line spacing at small font sizes.

## [1.2.2] - 2026-10-25

### Changed

- Add WoW Retail 12.1.7 to the supported interface versions.

## [1.2.1] - 2026-10-13

### Fixed

- Show all table entries in dumps instead of skipping entries after the first 30, and retain large dumps in Output.

## [1.2.0] - 2026-10-12

### Added

- Optional IntelliSense with keyboard navigation, Enter/Tab acceptance and parameter hints that remain visible while entering arguments. Request suggestions with Ctrl+Space without interrupting normal cursor navigation.
- Complete documented Blizzard APIs and enums, local variables, table members and functions, namespace aliases, and members and parameters from saved `requireHelper` modules.
- Move lines or selected blocks with Alt+Up/Down and duplicate them with Alt+Shift+Up/Down.
- Copy or cut the current line with native clipboard shortcuts when nothing is selected, and paste copied lines above the current line.
- Native macOS shortcuts: Command for editor actions and line/document navigation, Option for word navigation and line actions, and Shift to extend selections. Modified Backspace supports character, word and line deletion.

### Changed

- Typing an automatically inserted closing quote or bracket advances past it instead of inserting a duplicate.
- Use Shift+F12 to return from a definition jump, keeping Option+Arrow available for text navigation.

### Fixed

- Large scripts remain fully visible with consistent syntax colors and smoother typing and scrolling.
- Greatly reduce freezes when pasting large scripts into the editor.
- Keep the code editor focused when running a script with F5.
- Keep breakpoints aligned when inserting or joining lines, including blank lines and automatic indentation.
- Limit very large debug terminal outputs to prevent excessive processing and memory use.
